title: 2013 AMC 10B Problem 15

concepts.label: Power scaling of length, area, and volume

statement: A wire is cut into two pieces, one of length \(a\) and the other of length \(b.\) The piece of length \(a\) is bent to form an equilateral triangle, and the piece of length \(b\) is bent to form a regular hexagon. The triangle and the hexagon have equal area. What is \(\frac{a}{b}?\)

solutions.text:
Let \(s\) be the side length of the equilateral triangle and \(A\) its area. Then \(a=3s.\)

A regular hexagon of side length \(s\) consists of \(6\) equilateral triangles of side length \(s,\) so its area is \(6A.\)

Therefore, a regular hexagon of area \(A\) has side length \(\dfrac{s}{\sqrt 6} .\) Hence \[b = 6\cdot \dfrac{s}{\sqrt 6} = s\sqrt 6 .\]

It follows that \[\dfrac ab = \dfrac{3s}{s\sqrt 6} = \dfrac{3 \sqrt 6}6 = \dfrac{\sqrt 6} 2.\]

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Compare the side length of the large equilateral triangle with the small equilateral triangles inside the hexagon
Areas scale as the square of side length
